metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with Lambda entry points (src/payments/handlers.py), a dependency manifest (pyproject.toml), and single-service SAM IaC (infra/template.yaml).
metadata.archetype_justification: The service owns a persistent DynamoDB ledger and exposes write endpoints (POST /charges, POST /charges/{chargeId}/refunds) alongside a read endpoint; no queue consumers and no multi-service coordination.

top_gaps.question: OPS-Q9: Resource Tagging Governance
top_gaps.gap: No tags on any resource in infra/template.yaml.
top_gaps.impact: No cost allocation or ownership attribution for a payment-critical stack.

top_gaps.question: INF-Q11: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: CI validates and tests but never deploys; sam deploy is run by hand.
top_gaps.impact: Triggers Move to Modern DevOps; release is manual and unauditable.

top_gaps.question: OPS-Q5: Deployment Strategy
top_gaps.gap: No canary or traffic shifting; rollback is a manual redeploy of the prior artifact.
top_gaps.impact: A bad release reaches 100 percent of payment traffic immediately.

top_gaps.question: OPS-Q2: SLO Definitions
top_gaps.gap: Alarm thresholds exist in RUNBOOK.md prose only; no SLOs and no alarms in IaC.
top_gaps.impact: Service levels are not enforceable or reproducible.

top_gaps.question: APP-Q3: Async vs Sync Communication
top_gaps.gap: All processing is synchronous in-handler; no event emission on ledger writes.
top_gaps.impact: Downstream consumers must poll; no decoupled settlement path.

findings.title: Multi-step ledger write orchestrated in handler code
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated against the stateful-crud rubric, which expects a dedicated orchestrator for business-critical multi-step operations. The charge/refund flow is a hand-rolled sequence in _idempotent_put (get idempotency record, put ledger row, put idempotency row) with no AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine in IaC. Scored 2 rather than 1 because the sequence is small and clearly structured.
findings.gap: Sequencing and compensation live in application code; a crash between the two put_item calls leaves a ledger row with no idempotency record.
findings.recommendation: Make the write pair atomic with DynamoDB TransactWriteItems, or move reconcile/settlement multi-step flows to Step Functions with built-in retry and compensation.

findings.title: No managed messaging; synchronous design is currently correct
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated against the stateful-crud rubric. All reads and writes are synchronous API Gateway to Lambda, which is correct for this surface. No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Kinesis or MSK resources exist in infra/template.yaml, and no self-managed broker exists either. Scored 3 because no state change currently crosses a service boundary.
findings.gap: Ledger state changes emit no event, so a future settlement or notification consumer would have to poll the API.
findings.recommendation: Publish ChargeCreated/RefundCreated to EventBridge (or enable a DynamoDB stream) when the first consumer appears; do not introduce a broker before then.

findings.title: Strong transport controls, no WAF or managed networking layer
findings.description: Serverless surface with no VPC attachment, so there are no security groups or 0.0.0.0/0 rules. Ingress is limited to a regional custom domain terminating TLS 1.2+ with ACM, the raw execute-api endpoint is unpublished, and ReceiptsBucketPolicy denies non-TLS and sub-TLS-1.2 requests with full public-access block.
findings.gap: No managed networking services (VPC endpoints/PrivateLink) and no WAF on the API; function egress is unrestricted.
findings.recommendation: Attach AWS WAF to the API stage with rate-based rules; if VPC egress is later required, use private subnets with VPC endpoints for DynamoDB and S3.

findings.title: PITR and versioning enabled; no backup plan or restore drill
findings.description: The ledger has PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true and the receipts bucket has versioning enabled. No AWS::Backup::BackupPlan, no cross-region copy, and RUNBOOK.md documents no restore procedure or restore test.
findings.gap: Retention is limited to the PITR window with no long-term or cross-region copy, and the restore path has never been exercised.
findings.recommendation: Add an AWS Backup plan for the ledger with defined retention and cross-region copy, and document plus periodically exercise a restore procedure in RUNBOOK.md.

findings.title: CI validates but never deploys; release is a manual sam deploy
findings.description: ci.yml runs ruff, mypy, OpenAPI spec validation and pytest on push and pull request, but contains no sam build, no deploy job, and no rollback stage. RUNBOOK.md documents deployment as an operator running sam build && sam deploy --config-env prod.
findings.gap: Application and IaC changes are validated automatically but released manually, so the pipeline is not the deployment path and releases are not auditable.
findings.recommendation: Add a deploy job gated on the existing checks, assuming a deploy role via GitHub OIDC and running sam build && sam deploy --no-confirm-changeset with CodeDeploy-managed rollback.

findings.title: All communication synchronous for a state-owning service
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated against the stateful-crud rubric, which expects async propagation of cross-service state changes at the top score; a stateless-utility would have been recorded Not Evaluated, but this service owns and mutates a ledger. Every path in handlers.py is synchronous request/response and no publish call or event source mapping exists in code or IaC.
findings.gap: No asynchronous propagation of ledger state changes, and background work such as receipt generation has nowhere to run off the request path.
findings.recommendation: Emit domain events to EventBridge on charge and refund commit and move receipt writing to an async consumer, keeping the read path synchronous.

findings.title: No long-running operations today, and no async job surface if one appears
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated against the stateful-crud rubric. Functions are capped at Timeout: 15 and every operation is a small number of DynamoDB calls, so nothing approaches 30 seconds. There is also no async job framework, status endpoint, or checkpointing available.
findings.gap: No job-status surface or checkpointing exists, so a future bulk reconcile or export would have to block the caller.
findings.recommendation: Implement any future bulk reconcile or export as an async job (Step Functions or an SQS worker) returning a job id with a status endpoint, rather than extending the function timeout.

findings.title: Dependencies wired through environment variables, no discovery
findings.description: Resource references are injected by SAM as environment variables (LEDGER_TABLE via !Ref LedgerTable, COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID via !Ref UserPoolId) and read with os.environ. There is no service registry or Cloud Map usage, and also no hardcoded endpoints.
findings.gap: Environment-variable wiring with no dynamic discovery; each additional dependency requires more per-function parameter plumbing.
findings.recommendation: Keep env-var injection for in-stack resources, which is the correct serverless pattern, and adopt AWS Cloud Map or SSM Parameter Store lookups only once cross-stack service-to-service calls appear.

findings.title: Receipts in S3 with no parsing or extraction pipeline
findings.description: Settlement receipts are stored in a managed S3 bucket (ReceiptsBucket) with KMS default encryption, versioning and full public-access block. No Textract call, document parser, or extraction pipeline exists anywhere in src/payments/.
findings.gap: Objects are stored but never parsed or indexed, so receipt contents are not searchable or analyzable.
findings.recommendation: Add an S3 event-triggered extraction step (Textract or a structured-JSON receipt writer) and catalog the output if receipts need to be queried.

findings.title: Encryption everywhere, but on AWS-managed keys with no rotation policy
findings.description: Both at-rest surfaces are encrypted: LedgerTable sets SSESpecification SSEEnabled true and ReceiptsBucket uses SSEAlgorithm aws:kms with BucketKeyEnabled. No AWS::KMS::Key is declared and no KMSMasterKeyId is set, so both rely on AWS-managed keys with no documented rotation policy.
findings.gap: No customer-managed key, so there is no control over key policy, grants, or rotation for payment data.
findings.recommendation: Create a customer-managed KMS key with rotation enabled and reference it from the table SSESpecification.KMSMasterKeyId and the bucket ServerSideEncryptionByDefault.KMSMasterKeyID.

findings.title: No plaintext credentials anywhere; no managed store for future secrets
findings.description: No plaintext credential exists in the repository: no .env file, no password or api-key literals, no connection strings. Access is entirely IAM- and token-based (per-function DynamoDB read/write policies, OAuth2 bearer tokens that the code never persists or logs) and resource ids come from !Ref parameters. No Secrets Manager resource exists because the service currently holds no long-lived secret.
findings.gap: No managed secret store or rotation is in place for the day a payment-provider credential or webhook signing key is introduced.
findings.recommendation: Introduce AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation before the first provider credential or signing key is added, keeping non-secret resource ids in plain environment variables.

findings.title: Dependency patching automated; no vulnerability scanning
findings.description: dependabot.yml tracks pip and github-actions weekly with security labels. The runtime is an AWS-managed Lambda base (python3.12, arm64), so there is no AMI or container image to harden. No Inspector, no image scanning, and no SAST gate exist.
findings.gap: Patch automation covers declared dependencies only; no vulnerability scanning is integrated into the pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Enable Amazon Inspector Lambda scanning for the functions and add pip-audit to the CI workflow so advisories block a merge rather than arriving only as a pull request.

findings.title: Dependency scanning only; no SAST and no blocking security gate
findings.description: Dependency scanning runs via Dependabot and CI enforces ruff, mypy --strict and OpenAPI validation, but ci.yml contains no SAST tool, no pip-audit, and no step that fails the build on a security finding.
findings.gap: No static application security testing in the pipeline and no gate that blocks on a critical advisory.
findings.recommendation: Add a SAST step (bandit or Semgrep) and pip-audit to ci.yml, failing the job on high or critical findings.

findings.title: Alarm thresholds documented in prose, no SLOs or error budget
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md documents threshold alarms (payments-5xx above 1 percent over 5 minutes, payments-idempotency-conflict above 10 per minute, payments-ddb-throttle on any) and a payments-prod dashboard tracking p50/p99 latency and 4xx/5xx. No AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm resource exists in IaC and no named SLO, target, or error budget is defined.
findings.gap: Service levels are prose-only rather than declared in IaC, and no error budget is tracked.
findings.recommendation: Declare the runbook thresholds as CloudWatch alarms in the SAM template and define explicit availability and latency SLOs with error-budget tracking for the charge and refund journeys.

findings.title: One business metric published; refunds and conflicts unmeasured
findings.description: Powertools Metrics is configured with namespace Payments and create_charge emits a ChargeCreated count metric. refund_charge emits no metric and there is no metric for idempotency conflicts or refund volume, even though RUNBOOK.md alarms on conflicts.
findings.gap: Business metric coverage is partial, so one documented alarm has no emitted metric behind it.
findings.recommendation: Emit RefundCreated and IdempotencyConflict metrics, plus charge amount by currency, so the documented alarms and dashboard are backed by published metrics.

findings.title: Static threshold alarms only
findings.description: Alerting consists of the three fixed-threshold alarms described in RUNBOOK.md with a page-on-call action. No CloudWatch anomaly detection, no composite alarm, and no alarm resources in infra/template.yaml.
findings.gap: Fixed thresholds miss gradual degradation and novel failure modes on a payment path.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch anomaly detection bands on API latency and 5xx rate plus a composite alarm combining error rate with DynamoDB throttles, all declared in the SAM template.

findings.title: Direct-to-production releases with manual rollback
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md describes deployment as sam deploy --config-env prod with rollback by redeploying the previous immutable artifact. The template declares no AutoPublishAlias, no DeploymentPreference and no CodeDeploy configuration, so each release replaces the live version for all traffic with no canary and no alarm-triggered automatic rollback.
findings.gap: No traffic shifting and no automated rollback, so a regression reaches all payment traffic and recovery depends on a human redeploy.
findings.recommendation: Add AutoPublishAlias: live with DeploymentPreference Type Canary10Percent5Minutes and Alarms referencing the 5xx and idempotency-conflict alarms so a bad release rolls back automatically.

findings.title: Handler-level behavior tests in CI; nothing against a deployed stage
findings.description: tests/test_idempotency.py exercises the critical behaviors through the handler against a DynamoDB Local stub (retry does not double-charge, key reuse with a different body returns 409, missing scope is denied) and runs on every push and pull request alongside OpenAPI validation. Coverage stops at the handler boundary.
findings.gap: No post-deploy or contract test against the real API Gateway and authorizer path, so gateway and auth integration regressions are not caught.
findings.recommendation: Add a post-deploy smoke and contract test against the v1 stage covering a real token, an idempotent retry, and the 409 path, as a pipeline stage after the deploy job.

findings.title: Detailed runbook, but no automated remediation
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md is specific and operationally useful: dashboards, an alarm/threshold/action table, deploy and rollback commands, common operations including webhook replay, and a three-step escalation path. It is human-readable documentation only; no SSM Automation document, remediation Lambda, or self-healing workflow exists in IaC.
findings.gap: Every documented response step is executed manually; nothing is machine-executable or versioned as automation.
findings.recommendation: Convert the highest-frequency procedures such as webhook replay and idempotency-conflict triage into SSM Automation documents in IaC, and wire the 5xx alarm to an automated first-response action.

findings.title: Dashboards and alarms exist; ownership is informal
findings.description: A per-service dashboard (payments-prod), a named X-Ray service map, and three named alarms exist with a defined escalation target (Payments Platform), and the OpenAPI contact block names that team with a runbook URL. There is no CODEOWNERS file, no owner tag on observability resources, and the dashboard and alarms are not in IaC.
findings.gap: Ownership is documented informally rather than enforced through CODEOWNERS or team tags on observability assets.
findings.recommendation: Add a CODEOWNERS file covering infra/ and RUNBOOK.md, and tag dashboards and alarms with the owning team once they are declared in IaC.

findings.title: No tags on any provisioned resource
findings.description: infra/template.yaml provisions six resources (three Lambda functions, the API, the DynamoDB table, and the receipts bucket with its policy) and declares no Tags on any of them and no Globals.Function.Tags. There is no tagging standard, no Config rule, and not even a Name or owner tag.
findings.gap: No cost-allocation, ownership, or environment tags on a payment-critical stack, so spend cannot be attributed and incident ownership cannot be resolved from the resource.
findings.recommendation: Add Globals.Function.Tags plus per-resource Tags with consistent keys (Service, Owner, Environment, CostCenter) and enforce them with an AWS Config required-tags rule and an Organizations Tag Policy.

evaluations.title: Managed Compute
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - all compute is serverless Lambda (python3.12/arm64); no EC2 resources exist.

evaluations.title: Managed Databases
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - single managed DynamoDB table on PAY_PER_REQUEST with TTL, PITR and SSE; no self-managed engine.

evaluations.title: API Entry Point
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - API Gateway REST API with default Lambda authorizer and contract-first request validation from the OpenAPI spec.

evaluations.title: Auto-Scaling
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - Lambda concurrency and DynamoDB on-demand scale automatically; no static capacity to tune.

evaluations.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - all components (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB) are regional multi-AZ managed services.

evaluations.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - every exposed surface (compute, API, data, identity wiring) is declared in infra/template.yaml; the stack is the documented source of truth.

evaluations.title: Programming Languages
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - Python 3.12 with boto3 >=1.34, aws-lambda-powertools >=2.30 and mypy strict; runtime, framework and SDK all current.

evaluations.title: Monolith vs Microservices
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - independently deployable per-operation functions with least-privilege roles and explicit, non-circular module boundaries.

evaluations.title: API Versioning Strategy
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - single consistent scheme: v1 stage and URL path, OpenAPI server path and info.version aligned with the package version, spec validated in CI, closed schemas.

evaluations.title: Unified Data Access Layer
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - one module owns the DynamoDB client and the only write path; no other module imports boto3.

evaluations.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - DynamoDB is versionless and managed with no EOL exposure; the table is fully declared in IaC and the Lambda runtime is pinned.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - no SQL files, stored procedures, triggers or proprietary dialects; all business logic is in the application layer.

evaluations.title: API Authentication
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - DefaultAuthorizer applies OAuth2 client-credentials validation to every route, with per-operation scopes re-checked in handlers and covered by a test.

evaluations.title: Centralized Identity Integration
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - tokens are issued and validated against Cognito; no local user store or password handling exists.

evaluations.title: Distributed Tracing
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - X-Ray active on all functions and the API, Powertools Tracer instrumentation, and an X-Correlation-Id propagated into logs and every response.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Surface gate: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources is true but the IaC is application-level only (functions, API, table, bucket) with no account/foundation resources. CloudTrail is provisioned once per account or organization and belongs in the foundation infrastructure repo.

pathways.name: Move to Cloud Native
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary: APP-Q2 < 3, plus at least one of INF-Q1 < 3, APP-Q3 < 3, APP-Q4 < 3.

triggering_questions.note: APP-Q2 = 4; already independently deployable serverless functions, primary trigger not met
Supporting condition met but primary not met, so pathway does not fire

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Primary trigger APP-Q2 < 3 is not met: the service is already decomposed into per-operation Lambda functions.

pathways.name: Move to Containers
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary: INF-Q1 < 3 AND no container definitions found.
pathways.not_triggered_reason: Contextual guard applies: compute already runs on Lambda, so containerization is not the modernization step.

pathways.name: Move to Open Source
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary: DATA-Q4 < 3 AND commercial DB engines detected.

triggering_questions.note: DATA-Q4 = 4; no stored procedures or proprietary SQL
DynamoDB only; no commercial engine detected

pathways.not_triggered_reason: No proprietary SQL and no licensed database engine exist in the repository.

pathways.name: Move to Managed Databases

triggering_questions.note: INF-Q2 = 4; DynamoDB on-demand is fully managed
DATA-Q3 = 4; versionless managed engine, no EOL exposure

pathways.not_triggered_reason: The only datastore is already a fully managed service.

pathways.name: Move to Managed Analytics
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary: INF-Q4 < 3, with evidence of data processing workloads required by the guard.

triggering_questions.note: INF-Q4 = 3 meets threshold; synchronous design is correct for this archetype
Unified data access layer; no data source sprawl

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Contextual guard applies: no streaming, ETL, pipeline or analytics artifacts were found, and INF-Q4 meets the threshold.

pathways.name: Move to Modern DevOps
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary: INF-Q10 < 3 OR INF-Q11 < 3. INF-Q11 = 2 fired the pathway; OPS-Q5 = 2 strengthens it.

triggering_questions.note: Primary - CI validates and tests but has no build, deploy or rollback stage
Supporting - direct-to-production releases with manual rollback

detail.iac_coverage: INF-Q10 = 4; the full stack is declared in infra/template.yaml and is the documented source of truth, so IaC is not the gap.
detail.cicd_state: ci.yml runs ruff, mypy, OpenAPI validation and pytest on push/PR with no deploy or rollback stage; deployment is a manual sam deploy per RUNBOOK.md.
detail.deployment_gap: No AutoPublishAlias, DeploymentPreference or CodeDeploy configuration; releases replace the live version for all traffic.
detail.testing_gap: OPS-Q6 = 3; handler-level idempotency and scope tests run in CI, but nothing exercises a deployed stage.
immediate_actions: Add an OIDC-authenticated deploy job gated on the existing CI checks.
Add AutoPublishAlias: live with a Canary10Percent5Minutes DeploymentPreference and alarm-triggered rollback.
Promote the RUNBOOK.md alarm table into AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm resources in the SAM template.
Add a post-deploy smoke/contract test against the v1 stage.
Add required tags to all resources (OPS-Q9) as part of the same IaC pass.

pathways.name: Move to AI
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary: no AI/agent frameworks detected. Guard requires AI/agent/LLM intent evidenced in the repository.
pathways.not_triggered_reason: No AI/agent intent evidenced in the repository (no AI-related signal terms in dependencies, source, configuration, IaC, or documentation).
